title: Marine Atlantic Inc. – Port aux Basques Navigation Improvement Project
description: Marine Atlantic Inc. – Port aux Basques Navigation Improvement Project Notice of Request for Proposals Name of Procuring Entity:  Marine Atlantic Inc. (“MAI”) Contact Person:  Katie Clark, Director, Supply Chain Management ler2025@ma.ca Description of Procurement: Marine Atlantic Inc. is conducting a request for proposals (“RFP”) process for the removal of a landmass known as “Vardys Rock” and associated breakwater improvement (“Pikes I.”) both located in Port aux Basques Harbour in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada.  (See Canadian Hydrographic Service Chart #4641, Port aux Basques and Approaches/et les Approches, for location reference only. Note: Vardys Rock referenced as Vardys I.)  The project’s objective is to improve navigational constraints impacting Marine Atlantic’s operations and vessel maneuvering restrictions, in addition to the development of new land to improve harbour protection and enhance lobster habitat.   Work in this project will include the following:  •    The demolition and disposal of all miscellaneous structures, debris, and electrical components on Vardys Rock; •    The relocation and disposal of overburden on Vardys Rock to an offsite location; •    The removal of remaining earth materials and bedrock of and surrounding Vardys Rock to an elevation of -9.5m Chart Datum (with material relocation to an infill area adjacent to the nearby Pikes I.. The infill area will be reinforced by armourstone on all faces.   Construction will involve established marine techniques including drilling, blasting, dredging and excavation with material reused where possible to maximize efficiency and reduce waste.   Construction is expected to take approximately one year exclusive of removal of temporary infrastructure.   The RFP process will involve negotiation and will not involve an electronic auction. Procurement Documents: Prospective suppliers who are interested in participating in the RFP process are required to execute and return a confidentiality agreement in order to obtain access to the RFP documents and the data site that MAI will use for the RFP process. Prospective suppliers should email ler2025@ma.ca to request a copy of the confidentiality agreement.   Construction  Period: Completion of construction will be required by the end of Q1 2028.  Permitted Jurisdictions and Applicable Trade Agreements: This RFP process is being conducted in accordance with the Government of Canada's Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements and is therefore only open to Canadian Suppliers or Suppliers of an applicable trading partner as such terms are defined in such policy.  The government procurement agreements that apply to this procurement are the Canadian Free Trade Agreement, the Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership and the Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement.  Proponent Selection: MAI intends to conduct a prequalification as the first phase of the RFP and will prequalify up to three prequalified proponents who will participate in the second phase.  MAI intends to select a preferred proponent at the conclusion of the procurement process using a combined technical and financial score based on the following criteria. Organizational structure and project experience of Proponents providing similar services Proposed construction methodology inclusive of regulatory compliance, and effective measures so as to not impact harbour traffic and operations of Marine Atlantic Financial capacity; Pricing; The evaluation criteria are described in more detail in the RFP documents. Language of Submission:  Proposals are to be submitted in English. Address and Final Date for Submissions: Proposals must be submitted electronically on or before December 11, 2026 at 4:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time on the project data site.  The proposals will not be opened publicly. Single Proponent Structure: Proponent Team Members are only permitted to join a single Proponent.  This applies to all Proponent Team Members.  Notes: Prospective suppliers should note that information contained within this notice is subject to change. Prospective suppliers are encouraged to consult the RFP documents which contain the most current information.  If there is a conflict between the RFP documents and this notice, the RFP documents will take precedence.  Bidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. Fees may apply; See https://www.merx.com/public/pricing for more information.

description: Muuttopalvelujen sekä välivarastoinnin hankinta Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue sekä Vantaan kaupunki järjestävät tarjouskilpailun muuttopalvelujen sekä välivarastoinnin hankinnasta tämän tarjouspyynnön sekä sen liitteiden mukaisesti (VAKEDno-2026-2362 ja VD/3264/02.08.00.00/2026). Palvelu tuotetaan pääsääntöisesti Vantaan ja Keravan kaupunkien sekä Keski-Uudenmaan pelastuslaitoksen alueella. Hankinnan kohde on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteellä Palvelukuvaus. Muuttojen tilaaminen ei ole keskitettyä laajoissa tilaajaorganisaatioissa, joten yksittäisten muuttojen tilaajia voi olla useita tarpeesta riippuen. Hankinnalla tavoitellaankin yhteistyökumppania, joka on Tilaajien kokonaisvaltaisena tukena muuttojen valmistelussa sekä toteuttamisessa. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin. Hankinnassa valitaan yksi (1) Toimittaja. Hankintaa ei jaeta osiin. Hankintayksiköt ovat arvioineet hankinnan jakamista osiin hankinnan valmistelun yhteydessä tehdyn markkinavuoropuhelun perusteella. Selvityksen perusteella hankinnan kohde muodostaa käyttötarkoituksensa, toimeksiantojen yhteensovittamisen sekä vastuunjaon näkökulmasta yhden toiminnallisen kokonaisuuden. Hankinnan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena mahdollistaa palvelutuotannon ja sopimusvastuiden selkeän hallinnan yhden kokonaisvastuullisen sopimuskumppanin kautta. Tämän vuoksi hankinnan toteuttaminen yhtenä kokonaisuutena on hankinnan luonne ja hankintayksikön tarpeet huomioon ottaen perusteltua. Tilaajien ostot vuodelta 2025 olivat: Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue: noin 60 000 € alv 0 % vuodessa Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue toimeentulotuki- ja vammaispalvelun asiakkaiden muutot: noin 60 000 € alv 0 % vuodessa Vantaan kaupunki ja sen tytäryhtiöt: noin 400 000 alv 0 % vuodessa TIlaajat ei sitoudu hankintamääriin. Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialue julkaisee tämän tarjouspyynnön ja kilpailutuksen perusteella tehdään Vantaan kaupungille sekä Vantaan ja Keravan hyvinvointialueelle omat sopimukset kilpailutuksen voittaneen tarjoajan kanssa. Molemmat hankintayksiköt tekevät myös oman hankintapäätöksen. Vantaan kaupungin sopimuksen perusteella hankintoja voivat tehdä kaupungin kaikki toimialat sekä alla luetellut kaupungin enemmistöosuudella omistamat osakeyhtiöt: Vantaan Tilapalvelut Vantti Oy, VTK Kiinteistöt Oy- konserni, VAV Yhtymä Oy, VAV Asunnot Oy, VAV Palvelukodit Oy, VAV Hoivaasunnot Oy, Hakopolun Liikekiinteistö Oy, Kiinteistö Oy Hakucenter, Kiinteistö Oy Korson Toimistokeskus, Kiinteistö Oy Tikkurilan Terveysasema, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Helikopteritukikohta, Kiinteistö Oy Vantaan Maakotkantie 10, Pallastunturintien Liikekiinteistö Oy ja Asunto Oy Vantaan Katriinanrinne,

Vorhaltung Kamerasystem - 9 OP-Leuchte, LED (160 + 160 kLux), mit Kamerasystem - 7 OP-Leuchte, LED (160 + 160 kLux), mit Kamerasystem, unter LAF-Decke Inklusive der Schnittstelle (kompatible Steuerungsschnittstellen bzw. Software- /Hardwarekomponenten) zwischen den OP-Leuchten und dem bauseitigen Tableau (Touchscreen). Unterstützung zur Programmierung der Darstellung des Bedienfeldes im bauseitigen Tableau ist zu gewährleisten. Die Lieferung und Montage der Bestandteile soll nach dem folgenden Prioritäten-Schema getrennt ablaufen: Montage Unterkonstruktionen, Montage Leuchten, Lieferung Zubehör unmittelbar vor Inbetriebnahme (Diebstahlprävention). 1 Haupt- und 1 Nachbesserungstermin sind mit dem Angebotspreis abgegolten, wobei die Teilleistungen gemäß Terminplan gestaffelt einzutakten und mit der örtlichen Bauleitung/Fachbauleitung abzustimmen sind. Die gesetzliche Verjährungsfrist der Gewährleistungsansprüche beginnt mit der Abnahme der Leistung. Der Tag der Abnahme (komplette Montage inklusive Mängelbeseitigungen) ist der Gewährleistungsbeginn. Folgende Leistungen sind neben den gerätebezogenen Leistungen anzubieten und zu kalkulieren: - Bei der Kollisionsprüfung durch den koordinierenden Architekten (4Bund) ist durch den Auftragnehmer (AN) mitzuwirken. Die Montagepläne sind bei Erfordernis anzupassen. - Für Organisationsbesprechungen - auch teil- und abschnittsweise - hat der AN einen mit der Anlage in allen Teilen technisch und betrieblich vertrauten, sachkundigen Mitarbeiter beizustellen. - Weitere Leistungen gemäß den zusätzlichen technischen Vorbemerkungen der Medizintechnik. Für die Lieferungen und Montagen der Geräte sind folgende Termine maßgebend: Möglicher Beginn Einbau: 08.09.2027 Spätester Abschluss Montagen: 29.03.2029 (Innenausbau + Technik gem. Generalablaufplan_V5) Unter Berücksichtigung des Starttermins ist ein Montageterminplan vorzulegen und ggf. an Vorgaben des Architekten (4Bund) anzupassen. Die jeweils für die Einbringung und Montage benötigten Zeiten sind pro Gerät zu hinterlegen.

The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate and award a contract without providing for full and open competition (Including brand-name) to: Nikon Instruments Inc. 1300 Walt Whitman RD Melville, New York 11747 NORTH AMERICAN INDUSTRY CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM (NAICS) CODE The intended procurement is classified under NAICS code 811210 with a Size Standard $1000. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements. GENERAL INFORMATION Title: Replacement and Upgrade of Components for Three Nikon Live-Cell Imaging Systems Background Information: The National Cancer Institute (NCI), Center for Cancer Research (CCR), Laboratory of Cancer Biology and Genetics (LCBG) requires replacement of critical components for three existing Nikon live-cell epifluorescence imaging systems located in Dr. Steve Cappell's laboratory. These systems, installed between 2017 and 2019, support continuous, long-term live-cell imaging experiments used by multiple investigators within LCBG to study cell cycle regulation, cancer cell death, cancer stem cell biology, Ras signaling, and therapeutic responses. The imaging systems have experienced age-related degradation of key components, including scientific cameras, motorized filter wheels, workstation computers, and imaging software. Replacement of these components is necessary to restore instrument performance, maintain manufacturer support, extend the operational life of the systems, and minimize research disruptions. GENERAL INFORMATION Title: Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing laboratory services for genetic material binding analysis in mouse stem cells Background Information: The National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases is conducting research to better understand how the EXOSC10 protein contributes to genome stability during the repair of deoxyribonucleic acid damage. To support this research, the laboratory developed a mouse embryonic stem cell line in which the EXOSC10 protein contains a three-times FLAG tag, allowing the protein to be detected and enriched using an anti-FLAG antibody. Because the genome-wide binding pattern of EXOSC10 has not been fully characterized, antibody qualification is required before conducting chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing. Matched control cell lines expressing green fluorescent protein with the same three-times FLAG tag will be used to distinguish specific EXOSC10 binding from background signal and ensure reliable experimental results.. title: Land Survey Equipment - Trimble
description: 1. Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA805126Q4011 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a brand name only purchase for Trimble Inc. Land Survey Equipment. The Government intends to award one purchase order to the responsible offeror whose offer represents the Best Value to the Government. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Attachment 01 identifies clauses and provisions that apply to this RFQ. Offerors are required to complete all applicable representations and certifications found in the Clause Sheet (Attachment 1 - Clause Sheet), or ensure the Representations and Certifications are updated at www.sam.gov. All clauses and provisions may be found in full text at the following site https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide. The NAICS code for this acquisition is 334511 and the Small Business size standard is 1,350 employees. Attachment 02 includes all line items, including item descriptions, quantities, and units of measure. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). See Attachment 03 for shipping information including dates, location and F.O.B. point. 2. Responses. Vendor shall respond to this RFQ via email by 18 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. All quotes should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. 3. Questions. All questions regarding the RFQ package must be submitted to the below e-mail address by 14 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. Any questions received after this date and time may not be answered. Please note, only questions received in writing will be accepted. All releasable questions and answers will be provided by the Government in writing and posted publicly to SAM.gov under this RFQ. All questions should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. All offers must list their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, CAGE code, point of contact, and phone number. Vendors must also be registered in Wide Area Work Flow to receive payment through electronic funds transfer. If you are not currently registered, please visit the following website https://wawf.eb.mil/ to complete your registration. 4. Organizational Conflicts of Interest: All offerors shall identify any conflict of interest or appearance issues that might be a potential Organizational Conflict of Interest. 5. Notice to Offerors: The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFQ, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. Submitted offers shall be valid for 60 calendar days after the closing date of the RFQ. 7. Additional Instructions. A commercial small business subcontracting plan is required in accordance with FAR 52.219-9 - Small Business Subcontracting Plan. Prior to award, the Government will request an approved commercial plan from the apparent successful offeror. If an approved commercial plan does not exist, one will be negotiated and approved prior to award. The small business goals for negotiated plans are included in the table below. This requirement does not apply to small business concerns. Small Business: 30% of total subcontracting dollars Small Disadvantaged Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars Woman Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars HUBZone Small Business: 3% of total subcontracting dollars Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars 6. Best Value Evaluation. For this procurement, the Best Value determination will be made as Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: A) Price and B) Technical. The Government intends to award to the contractor with the lowest price who meets the technical requirements of the RFQ. The responses to this RFQ are intended to be evaluated, and award made, without discussions unless discussions are deemed to be necessary. The Government will sort quote from lowest to highest based on the total evaluated price (TEP). Once the quotes are sorted by TEP the technical evaluations will begin starting with the lowest priced quote. Technical evaluations will continue until the Contracting Officer determines 1) that a sufficient number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to establish price fair and reasonable based on adequate competition and 2) a significant number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to reduce the risk to the Government if the LPTA offeror fails to perform in accordance with the contract and order specifications. Once the contracting officer determines the above criteria have been met, all further technical evaluations will cease. The following process will be followed: A. Price. Use Attachment 02 to provide unit pricing. TEP will be determined by multiplying the unit costs by the quantities identified in Attachment 02. B. Technical: To be determined technically acceptable, offerors must provide the exact Trimble brand survey equipment listed in Attachment 02. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). Delivery will be FOB Destination and quotes must include delivery date information. C. Past performance will be evaluated as acceptable or unacceptable. Past performance for each offeror will be verified by reviewing the Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS) and the offeror�s Supplier Risk Score in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) (IAW DFARS 252.204-7024). Acceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has no negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years and no negative relevant information in SPRS. A lack of Past Performance will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably and will therefore be evaluated as Acceptable. Unacceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years or negative relevant information SPRS. Evaluation of Options. The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise any option(s). Attachments: 1.Q4011 Atch 1 Clauses 2.Q4011 Atch 2 Line Item Pricing 3.Q4011 Atch 3 Shipping Info 4.Q4011 Atch 4 Brand Name Only Justification

title: Octet� R4 to Octet� R8 Upgrade
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Sartorius for an Octet� R4 to Octet� R8 Upgrade. The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Government requires an upgrade of its existing Octet R4 Bio-Layer Interferometry (BLI) instrument to an Octet R8 configuration to increase sample capacity, efficiency, and throughput. The upgrade will double the instrument's sample capacity per run, allowing more comprehensive data collection in a single analysis session and reducing the need for multiple runs. The upgrade will also include an evaporation cover to minimize sample evaporation and preserve samples following analysis. The required upgrade must be compatible with and installed on the Government's existing Octet R4 instrument. Based on the proprietary nature of the existing system and the unique configuration and compatibility requirements of the upgrade, Sartorius is the only known responsible source capable of providing the required Octet R4-to-R8 upgrade without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delay. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they are capable of meeting the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required upgrade and meet all technical, compatibility, and installation requirements. The Government will consider all timely responses received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01175 in the subject line of the response.

The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Attachment 01 identifies clauses and provisions that apply to this RFQ. Offerors are required to complete all applicable representations and certifications found in the Clause Sheet (Attachment 1 - Clause Sheet), or ensure the Representations and Certifications are updated at www.sam.gov. All clauses and provisions may be found in full text at the following site https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide. The NAICS code for this acquisition is 334511 and the Small Business size standard is 1,350 employees. Attachment 02 includes all line items, including item descriptions, quantities, and units of measure. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). See Attachment 03 for shipping information including dates, location and F.O.B. point. 2. Responses. Vendor shall respond to this RFQ via email by 18 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. All quotes should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. 3. Questions. All questions regarding the RFQ package must be submitted to the below e-mail address by 14 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. Any questions received after this date and time may not be answered. Please note, only questions received in writing will be accepted. All releasable questions and answers will be provided by the Government in writing and posted publicly to SAM.gov under this RFQ. All questions should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. All offers must list their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, CAGE code, point of contact, and phone number. Vendors must also be registered in Wide Area Work Flow to receive payment through electronic funds transfer. If you are not currently registered, please visit the following website https://wawf.eb.mil/ to complete your registration. 4. Organizational Conflicts of Interest: All offerors shall identify any conflict of interest or appearance issues that might be a potential Organizational Conflict of Interest. 5. Notice to Offerors: The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFQ, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. Submitted offers shall be valid for 60 calendar days after the closing date of the RFQ. 7. Additional Instructions. A commercial small business subcontracting plan is required in accordance with FAR 52.219-9 - Small Business Subcontracting Plan. Prior to award, the Government will request an approved commercial plan from the apparent successful offeror. If an approved commercial plan does not exist, one will be negotiated and approved prior to award. The small business goals for negotiated plans are included in the table below. This requirement does not apply to small business concerns. Small Business: 30% of total subcontracting dollars Small Disadvantaged Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars Woman Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars HUBZone Small Business: 3% of total subcontracting dollars Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars 6. Best Value Evaluation. For this procurement, the Best Value determination will be made as Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: A) Price and B) Technical. The Government intends to award to the contractor with the lowest price who meets the technical requirements of the RFQ. The responses to this RFQ are intended to be evaluated, and award made, without discussions unless discussions are deemed to be necessary. The Government will sort quote from lowest to highest based on the total evaluated price (TEP). Once the quotes are sorted by TEP the technical evaluations will begin starting with the lowest priced quote. Technical evaluations will continue until the Contracting Officer determines 1) that a sufficient number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to establish price fair and reasonable based on adequate competition and 2) a significant number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to reduce the risk to the Government if the LPTA offeror fails to perform in accordance with the contract and order specifications. Once the contracting officer determines the above criteria have been met, all further technical evaluations will cease. The following process will be followed: A. Price. Use Attachment 02 to provide unit pricing. TEP will be determined by multiplying the unit costs by the quantities identified in Attachment 02. B. Technical: To be determined technically acceptable, offerors must provide the exact Trimble brand survey equipment listed in Attachment 02. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). Delivery will be FOB Destination and quotes must include delivery date information. C. Past performance will be evaluated as acceptable or unacceptable. Past performance for each offeror will be verified by reviewing the Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS) and the offeror�s Supplier Risk Score in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) (IAW DFARS 252.204-7024). Acceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has no negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years and no negative relevant information in SPRS. A lack of Past Performance will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably and will therefore be evaluated as Acceptable. Unacceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years or negative relevant information SPRS. Evaluation of Options. The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise any option(s). title: EVOS� M5000 Imaging System
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thermo Fisher Scientific for an EVOS� M5000 Imaging System. The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The Laboratory of Cancer Biology and Genetics (LCBG) requires an integrated imaging system to support ongoing NIH-funded research involving pancreatic cancer, including brightfield and fluorescence imaging, immunofluorescence analysis, transwell migration assays, live-cell imaging, bacterial-host interaction studies, and quantitative analysis of tissue specimens. The required system must provide immediate, standardized brightfield and fluorescence imaging capabilities within the laboratory to support time-sensitive live-cell and fluorescent specimen imaging and reduce dependence on shared microscopy facilities. The Government requires the following: One (1) EVOS� M5000 Imaging System, equipped with a 3.2-megapixel scientific-grade monochrome camera and 18.5-inch articulated LCD monitor. One (1) EVOS� Objective Starter Kit, containing 4X, 10X, and 20X fluorite long-working-distance objectives for brightfield, phase contrast, and fluorescence imaging. The EVOS� M5000 was identified as the only commercially available system that meets the Government's complete combination of functional, technical, operational, and workflow requirements as an integrated platform without requiring additional third-party hardware, software, or custom configuration. Other systems evaluated may provide individual comparable components but require additional hardware, separate computers, third-party software, or extensive configuration to provide equivalent functionality. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they can meet the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide a system meeting all specified technical and operational requirements. The Government will consider all timely capability statements received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01178 in the subject line of the response.

title: Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) 320 nm Laser for High-Dimensional Flow Cytometry.
description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Coherent Corporation for a Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) 320 nm Laser for High-Dimensional Flow Cytometry. The LP Research Flow Cytometry Facility provides essential cell sorting and flow cytometry analysis services to the Experimental Transplantation and Immunotherapy Branch and other branches and programs within the Center for Cancer Research (CCR). The required 320 nm deep ultraviolet laser is necessary to upgrade existing high-dimensional flow cytometers and enable excitation of deep-ultraviolet fluorescent probes. The laser will expand the laboratory's high-dimensional analysis capabilities without requiring the purchase of an entirely new flow cytometer. The unit must be capable of installation and use with the laboratory's existing Cytek spectral, LSR II, LSR Fortessa, and Influx flow cytometers, as applicable. The expanded capability will support validation of deep-ultraviolet fluorochromes, their integration into existing panels, and their continued use in research applications. The Government intends to solicit from a single source in accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Based on the proprietary nature, unique configuration, and compatibility requirements of the equipment, Coherent Corporation is the only known responsible source capable of providing the required laser without substantial duplication of cost or unacceptable delay. This notice is not a request for competitive quotations. However, interested parties that believe they are capable of meeting the Government's requirements may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to provide the required 320 nm deep ultraviolet laser and meet the Government's technical and compatibility requirements. The Government will consider all timely responses received and determine whether the acquisition should proceed as a sole-source procurement or be competed. The Government anticipates making an award approximately five (5) calendar days after the closing date of this notice, unless the Government determines that another responsible source is capable of meeting the requirement. Capability statements shall be submitted electronically to haunp@mail.nih.gov no later than 9:00 a.m. EDT on September 18, 2026. Please reference Notice No. 75N98026Q01174 in the subject line of the response.

title: Unified Application Access and Integration Prototype
description: DCSA INNOVATION GATEWAY INNOVATION CALL #01 Unified Application Access and Integration Prototype This is Innovation Call #01 under the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Innovation Gateway (HS0021-26-CSO-DCSA). Requirement Title Unified Application Access and Integration Prototype Problem Statement DCSA�s mission operations for personnel vetting, industrial security, counterintelligence, and insider-threat activities are supported by multiple separate applications that users must navigate to complete related work. This fragmented environment creates disconnected workflows, inconsistent authentication and user experiences, and inefficient access paths that increase user burden and reduce operational efficiency. It also adds complexity to the sustainment, modification, and modernization of mission applications and services. DCSA requires a more unified and user-centered approach that improves workflow continuity and usability while preserving continuity of operations for existing Individual Engagement (IE) applications during prototype development and evaluation. The underlying challenge is to transition from siloed legacy capabilities to an integrated platform of modular components that can support phased integration, replacement, and modernization of back-end services without disrupting the user experience or mission execution. description: This Request for Information (RFI) initiates market research under Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 10 to support planning for the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Defensive Cyber Systems Branch (HNCD), Joint Base San Antonio�Lackland, TX. PURPOSE This is a Request for Information for the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) Defensive Cyber Systems Branch (HNCD). The purpose of this RFI is to conduct market research to identify commercial sources capable of providing a Next-Generation, Vendor-Agnostic Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) software solution. The program office is seeking industry feedback on software solutions that meet or exceed the capabilities of enterprise orchestration platforms like Palo Alto Cortex XSOAR. The desired platform must avoid vendor ecosystem lock-in, support highly extensible modular open architectures, and be capable of deployment across enterprise cloud, garrison, and localized tactical edge environments on standard commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) computing baselines (referred to as the V+ platform architecture). The government intends to evaluate solutions that offer robust, decentralized orchestration, a vast open-integration marketplace, native threat intelligence lifecycle management, and advanced Machine Learning (ML)-assisted analyst workflows. title: Land Survey Equipment - Trimble
description: 1. Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number FA805126Q4011 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for a brand name only purchase for Trimble Inc. Land Survey Equipment. The Government intends to award one purchase order to the responsible offeror whose offer represents the Best Value to the Government. This acquisition is not set-aside for small business concerns. The solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Attachment 01 identifies clauses and provisions that apply to this RFQ. Offerors are required to complete all applicable representations and certifications found in the Clause Sheet (Attachment 1 - Clause Sheet), or ensure the Representations and Certifications are updated at www.sam.gov. All clauses and provisions may be found in full text at the following site https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul/far-part-deviation-guide. The NAICS code for this acquisition is 334511 and the Small Business size standard is 1,350 employees. Attachment 02 includes all line items, including item descriptions, quantities, and units of measure. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). See Attachment 03 for shipping information including dates, location and F.O.B. point. 2. Responses. Vendor shall respond to this RFQ via email by 18 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. All quotes should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. 3. Questions. All questions regarding the RFQ package must be submitted to the below e-mail address by 14 September 2026 at 0800 Central Time. Any questions received after this date and time may not be answered. Please note, only questions received in writing will be accepted. All releasable questions and answers will be provided by the Government in writing and posted publicly to SAM.gov under this RFQ. All questions should be sent to the Contracting Officer, Grace Pennington, at grace.pennington@us.af.mil before the due date and time specified. All offers must list their Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number, CAGE code, point of contact, and phone number. Vendors must also be registered in Wide Area Work Flow to receive payment through electronic funds transfer. If you are not currently registered, please visit the following website https://wawf.eb.mil/ to complete your registration. 4. Organizational Conflicts of Interest: All offerors shall identify any conflict of interest or appearance issues that might be a potential Organizational Conflict of Interest. 5. Notice to Offerors: The Government reserves the right to cancel this RFQ, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels this solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs. Submitted offers shall be valid for 60 calendar days after the closing date of the RFQ. 6. Additional Instructions. An Offeror�s quote must demonstrate they are an authorized supplier of the equipment and incidental services listed in Attachment 02 Line Item Pricing. In order to demonstrate an Offeror is an authorized supplier for this requirement, Offerors shall provide an authorized supplier letter from the OEM indicating they are an authorized supplier for solicitation FA805126Q4011. Not providing an authorized supplier letter from the OEM will result in the quote being evaluated as technically unacceptable and ineligible for award. A commercial small business subcontracting plan is required in accordance with FAR 52.219-9 - Small Business Subcontracting Plan. Prior to award, the Government will request an approved commercial plan from the apparent successful offeror. If an approved commercial plan does not exist, one will be negotiated and approved prior to award. The small business goals for negotiated plans are included in the table below. This requirement does not apply to small business concerns. Small Business: 30% of total subcontracting dollars Small Disadvantaged Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars Woman Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars HUBZone Small Business: 3% of total subcontracting dollars Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business: 5% of total subcontracting dollars 7. Best Value Evaluation. For this procurement, the Best Value determination will be made as Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA). The following factors will be used to evaluate offers: A) Price and B) Technical. The Government intends to award to the contractor with the lowest price who meets the technical requirements of the RFQ. The responses to this RFQ are intended to be evaluated, and award made, without discussions unless discussions are deemed to be necessary. The Government will sort quotes from lowest to highest based on the total evaluated price (TEP). Once the quotes are sorted by TEP the technical evaluations will begin starting with the lowest priced quote. Technical evaluations will continue until the Contracting Officer determines 1) that a sufficient number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to establish price fair and reasonable based on adequate competition and 2) a significant number of quotes have been determined technically acceptable to reduce the risk to the Government if the LPTA offeror fails to perform in accordance with the contract and order specifications. Once the contracting officer determines the above criteria have been met, all further technical evaluations will cease. The following process will be followed: A. Price. Use Attachment 02 to provide unit pricing. TEP will be determined by multiplying the unit costs by the quantities identified in Attachment 02. B. Technical: To be determined technically acceptable, offerors must provide the exact Trimble brand survey equipment listed in Attachment 02 and demonstrate they are an authorized supplier of the equipment and incidental services listed in Attachment 02 Line Item Pricing. This is a brand name only requirement in accordance with FAR 6.302-1. The brand name only justification is attached to this RFQ (Attachment 04). Delivery will be FOB Destination and quotes must include delivery date information. C. Past performance will be evaluated as acceptable or unacceptable. Past performance for each offeror will be verified by reviewing the Federal Awardee Performance and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS) and the offeror�s Supplier Risk Score in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) (IAW DFARS 252.204-7024). Acceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has no negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years and no negative relevant information in SPRS. A lack of Past Performance will not be evaluated favorably or unfavorably and will therefore be evaluated as Acceptable. Unacceptable past performance will be determined if the offeror has negative relevant past performance information in FAPIIS within the last five years or negative relevant information SPRS. Evaluation of Options. The Government will evaluate offers for award purposes by adding the total price for all options to the total price for the basic requirement. The Government may determine that an offer is unacceptable if option prices are significantly unbalanced. Evaluation of options shall not obligate the Government to exercise any option(s). description: The National Research Council of Canada's (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation, part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory, has a requirement for the supply of one (1) battery-electric, heavy-lift vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) remotely piloted aircraft system (RPAS) for Arctic and harsh-environment operations, the GRIFF 30, including the aircraft with one set of batteries, two (2) additional operational batteries, a battery charger, a ground control station, a cargo hook, satellite-based command-and-control (C2) integration, and manufacturer-provided flight and maintenance training.

title: Switzerland – Architectural and related services – Ausbildungszentrum Riedikon, Neubau Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum
description: Auf dem Grundstück Kat.-Nr. L1340, Bühlenweg 20 in Riedikon, betreibt die Leistungsgruppe Bevölkerungsschutz der Stadt Uster ein Ausbildungszentrum. Die Grundstücksfläche umfasst total 28'573 m2, wovon für das Ausbildungszentrum 10'400 m2, für die Vermietung an den Hundeclub 4600 m2 und für die landwirtschaftliche Verpachtung 9300 m2 genutzt werden. 4273 m2 sind Restfläche mit Wald und Moor. Das Ausbildungszentrum besteht aus diversen Übungsgebäuden und -flächen, sowie den zugehörigen Garderoben-, Schulungs-, Verwaltungs- und Lagerräumen. Die beiden Brandhäuser wurden in den vergangenen Jahren neu erstellt und sind auf dem neuesten Stand. Die Nebengebäude sind teilweise in einem schlechten Zustand und dringend sanierungsbedürftig. Mit dem Unterpachtvertrag für das Areal Zeughaus West an eine gemeinnützige Wohnbaugenossenschaft muss der Zivilschutz in absehbarer Zeit dieses Areal verlassen und benötigt neue Einstellflächen für die Fahrzeuge und einen Ort für den Zusammenzug. Aus diesen beiden Gründen wurde entschieden, das Ausbildungszentrum um ein neues Logistik- und Verwaltungszentrum zu erweitern. So kann der gesamte Zivilschutz an einem zentralen Ort untergebracht und Schulungen abgehalten werden.

This Procurement exercise and the subsequent Service to be commissioned will cover only the Northern Ireland delivery Lot Areas, which will be located within the boundaries of the Southern Health and Social Care Trust (SHSCT) and Western Health and Social Care Trust (WHSCT). The Service will involve the delivery of Tier 1 Community-Based Early Intervention Support for Adults in the following areas: Increasing Physical Activity and reducing sedentary behaviour; Healthy Eating; and Behaviour Change. Please refer to the full suite of tender documents for further information on the Service requirements. title: Biometric Capture Device GWAC
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12 in conjunction with the procedures, as appropriate, at RFO FAR Part 15, and as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation is hereby issued as part of this notice. The anticipated Biometric Capture Devices solicitation shall be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) where RFO FAR provision 52.212-1 and clause 52.212-4 apply. Additional provisions, clauses, terms and conditions, to include evaluation factors and the basis for award, are in the Solicitation. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Procurement Operations (OPO) issues this Request for Proposals (RFP) to establish government-wide, multiple-award indefinite-delivery indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contracts for biometric capture devices and peripheral equipment. The IDIQ contracts will permit Firm Fixed-Price orders. The period of performance will consist of a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. The dates of the periods of performance will be established at contract award. See Section F. The Biometric Capture Devices solicitation will be available for full and open competition with the anticipation that multiple awards will be made within each of the five (5) device tracks, Fingerprint, Facial, Iris, Palmprint, and Multi-Modal. For each track, the Government anticipates establishing a minimum of three (3) and maximum of unlimited IDIQ contracts with Offerors submitting an overall proposal that is determined to be best value to the Government utilizing a Highest Technically Rated with a Fair and Reasonable Price award basis. These numbers are estimates, and DHS may increase or decrease the number of awards in its sole discretion. In determining the number of awards, DHS�s intent is to ensure beneficial competition occurs at the delivery order level while maximizing the effectiveness and efficiency of the BCD program. Proposal submission and evaluation details are provided within Sections L and M of this solicitation. Multiple Proposals Interested offerors may submit proposals for one or more of the five BCD award tracks. Each award track requires a separate proposal. Accordingly, an offeror that wishes to compete under multiple tracks shall submit a separate proposal for each track. Within a single track, an offeror may propose more than one device that satisfies the requirements of that track. In that case, the offeror shall include all proposed devices for that track within the single proposal submitted for that track. Offerors shall clearly identify the applicable award track in the proposal cover letter. Alternate proposals with differing pricing models or technologies from those required in this solicitation will not be accepted or evaluated. Basis for Award Proposals shall be submitted in accordance with the instructions outlined in Section L. Proposals that fail to comply with proposal submission requirements may be removed from further evaluation or consideration for award. The Government anticipates awarding a minimum of three (3) IDIQ contracts beneath each track (Fingerprint, Face, Iris, Palm, Multi-Modal) to those responsible Offerors whose proposals are most advantageous and represent the best value to the Government utilizing the Highest Technically Rated Offerors with a Fair and Reasonable Price (HTRO-FRP) award basis. There is no maximum number of IDIQ awards per track. These numbers are estimates, and DHS may increase or decrease the number of awards in its sole discretion. Using the HTRO-FRP award basis, the Government will evaluate the non-price factors to first determine the highest technically rated proposals beneath each track. The Government will then evaluate price for those Offerors determined to be among the highest technically rated proposals within each track to determine whether their proposed prices are fair and reasonable. The Government will select for award within each track the highest technically rated offerors with fair and reasonable pricing. If an offeror submits a proposal with multiple devices under a single track, each device will be separately evaluated and considered for award using a HTRO-FRP award basis. To be clear, the Government will not consider tradeoffs between price and non-price factors under the HTRO-FRP award basis. The Evaluation Factors are as follows: Factor 1 � Availability of Devices Factor 2 - Supporting Documentation (Not Rated) Factor 3 � Technical Approach Factor 4 � Price (Not Rated) Proposal Submission Proposals shall be submitted via e-mail to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist on or before September 18, 2026 at 10:00 AM Eastern Time. Question Submission All questions associated with the subject solicitation shall be sent in writing to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 10:00AM Eastern Time on September 14, 2026.

This Request for Quotation (RFQ) HT940626QE086 is a sole source for the delivery, installation, and maintenance for an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors in support of the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. Notice of Intent The Defense Health Agency (DHA) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis in accordance with FAR part 12.102(a). For purchases not exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold, only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand name, or industrial mobilization). The proposed source is Securitas Technology Corporation, 3800 Tabs Drive, Uniontown, OH 44685-9564. This acquisition is for the procurement of an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors, to include all-inclusive labor, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors with the existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware utilized by the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. It is the contractor�s responsibility to be familiar with the applicable FAR and DFARS clauses and provisions. The FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed in full text at the below-referenced addresses: FAR Clauses: https://www.acquisition.gov/browse/index/far FAR Overhaul: https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul DFARS Clauses: https://www.acguisition.gov/dfars The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Codes: 561621 � Security Alarm Systems Sales Combined with Installation, Repair, or Monitoring Services This acquisition is for the procurement of an additional twenty-one (21) access control doors, to include all-inclusive labor, personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and non-personal services necessary to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors with the existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware utilized by the 45th Medical Group (MDG), Patrick, Space Force Base (SFB), FL. The 21 access control doors must be integrated with the current existing Securitas server and Lenel software infrastructure and hardware for system programming and control. The contractor shall be responsible for the configuration of the new 21 access control doors with the existing Lenel software across multiple facilities/buildings within the 45th MDG. All access-controlled doors must be programmed to lock or unlock based on a time schedule provided through the Lenel software system integrated with the Securitas Technology server. Only Securitas Technology Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) certified and qualified technicians are authorized to perform the installation and integration of the 21 access control doors and service the Lenel software infrastructure and hardware. All installation, integration, software licensing, warranty, and services associated with the 21 access control doors, Lenel software, and all equipment shall be in accordance with OEM terms and conditions. The contractor shall provide installation and integration of the 21 access control doors and all services during normal business hours (i.e., 8 hours a day and 5 days a week), excluding United States Federal Government holidays, which are identified online at the following site: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federa1-holidays/#url=2026. Reference the Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the required tasks and qualifications required for this requirement. The solicitation number is: HT940626QE086. Instructions to Vendors This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for the requirement; however, if a vendor challenges the basis for this requirement, please submit a capability statement that includes sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to submit a product meeting the minimum requirements specified above. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 12-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information or submission that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a sole source procurement. Responses Submission Capability statements are due by 10:00 A.M. ET, 2 September 2026. Capability statements shall be submitted by email ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to derrick.w.walker.civ@health.mil and jessica.l.horst5.civ@health.mil. No phone calls will be accepted.

title: MARSOC Advance Training Company (ATC)
description: Action: Notice of Intent to Sole Source Agency: U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) Contracting Office: Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) Classification Code: NAICS: 541611 � Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services PSC: R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Subject: Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract for Marine Raider Training Center (MRTC) Advance Training Company (ATC) Full Time Equivalent (FTE). 1. Description of Requirement: The U.S. Marine Corps Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC) intends to award a single-award Definitive Contract to Threat Tec LLC to provide precise and effective special reconnaissance operations that are fully coordinated and synchronized among all components of USSOCOM and key interagency organizations. The ATC program requires contracted support for exercise design, development, and management, scenario constructions, and tailored training support. The contractor shall provide formal training to individual Critical Skills Operators (CSO) in Advanced SR skills to provide qualified CSO�s to the Marine Special Operations Companies (MSOCs). The unit specifically charged with this responsibility is the MRTC. Due to the small size of the MRTC staff, contractor assistance is required to support the Special Reconnaissance, Instructor Sustainment Courses, and other Advanced SR Courses. The resultant contract will have a one-year basis for a total estimated price of $2,994,950.40. 2. Authority: This action is being conducted on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR Overhaul 6.103-1 for the acquisition of noncommercial services using Negotiated Contracting Procedures under RFO Part 15. 3. Rationale for Sole Source: Threat Tec, LLC is the incumbent contractor currently executing the MRTC ATC course curriculum, exercise design, full-mission profiles, and scenario development. An immediate bridge is required to prevent catastrophic lapses in specialized training pipelines for Marines Special Operations Companies (MSOCs) and Critical Skills Operators (CSOs) deploying to global operational areas. This bridge contract is essential to prevent a critical gap in mission-essential training services while USSOCOM finalizes, awards, and fully implements its comprehensive, enterprise-wide SOF Global Services Delivery (SOFGSD) contract in the fiscal year of 2027. SOFGSD will replace the prior SOF Core Support Services contract. The contract covers the full range of knowledge-based services supporting U.S.-based and globally assigned Special Operations Forces, from training and program management to intelligence support engineering and administrative services. Awarding an alternate contractor for this interim bridge period would introduce substantial, mission-degrading delays. The advanced ATC curriculum requires cleared, highly vetted personnel with existing institutional knowledge of MARFORSOC and USSOCOM Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs). Any phase-in/ramp-up period would compromise active, scheduled course iterations. Transitioning to a new vendor for an interim period prior to onboarding onto the SOFGSD vehicle would result in significant duplicate mobilization and phase-in costs that cannot be recovered through competition. 4. Notice to Industry: All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation within fifteen (15) calendar days of publication of this notice, which shall be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Capability statements received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in lieu of this sole-source action. 5. Submission Instructions: All capability statements must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer, Jordan D. Orellana Buitron, at jordan.d.orellanabuitron.mil@socom.mil and Contracting Specialist, Ger Yang, at ger.yang.mil@socom.mil.

title: Caméras de sécurité et contrôle d'accès
Netherlands – Firefighting, rescue and safety equipment – Warmtebeeldcamera's t.b.v. Brandweer Twente
description: De VRT wenst per perceel één Opdrachtnemer te contracteren voor de levering van warmtebeeldcamera’s (WBC’s) en bijbehorende toebehoren. De WBC’s worden ingezet ter ondersteuning van brandbestrijding, technische hulpverlening en incidentbestrijding en dragen bij aan de veiligheid en effectiviteit van hulpverleners tijdens operationele inzet. De aanbesteding omvat de volgende percelen: • Perceel 1 – Decision Making Camera: warmtebeeldcamera voor gebruik onder zware en extreme omstandigheden, met nadruk op hittebestendigheid, robuustheid en besluitvorming tijdens inzet. • Perceel 2 – Situational Awareness Camera: persoonlijke warmtebeeldcamera voor oriëntatie in rook, detectie van thermische sporen en ondersteuning van de individuele veiligheid, met minimale bediening en een gewicht van maximaal 500 gram. Onder WBC’s en toebehoren worden verstaan: accessoires, laders, accu’s, software, onderhouds- en reparatiemogelijkheden, technische ondersteuning, updates en training. Raamovereenkomst; geen gegarandeerde afname.

title: Continuous Improvement of two CGE Models
description: 1. Summary Environment and Climate Change Canada has a requirement for on demand technical support and expertise for the continuous improvement of two established CGE models used to assess climate policy impacts. The two models are EC-PRO and EC-MSMR as detailed in the Statement of Work, Annex A to the bid solicitation. The period of the Contract is for three years from date of Contract Award. 2. Security There is no security requirement associated with this solicitation. 3. Integrity Provisions Bidders must provide a list of names, or other related information as needed, pursuant to section 01 Integrity Provisions of Standard Instructions 2003. 4. Reciprocal Procurement - Limited Supplier Eligibility Solicitation of Offer Submission Eligibility. This solicitation of offers is subject to the Policy on Reciprocal Procurement. This means that only Canadian Suppliers and Suppliers of an Applicable Trading Partner, as defined in the Attachment 1 to Part 1 Solicitation of Offers Definitions, are eligible for this solicitation of offers. Offers submitted by Suppliers of a Non-Trading Partner will be rejected. 5. Service Requirements For services requirements, bidders in receipt of a pension or a lump sum payment must provide the required information as detailed in article 3 of Part 2 of the bid solicitation. 6. Trade Agreements The requirement is subject to the provisions of the of the Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), the Canada–Chile Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement, the Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, the Comprehensive Economic Free Trade Agreement [CETA], the World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement [WTO-AGP], the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership [CPTPP] and the Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement. 7. Social Procurement Environment and Climate Change Canada supports the Government of Canada’s social and economic objectives, including increasing the participation of businesses from under-represented groups in government procurement opportunities. As such, bidders owned or led by Canadians from under-represented groups, such as women, LGBTQ2+ persons, persons with disabilities and persons from visible minorities are encouraged to submit a bid to this opportunity. 8. Debriefings Bidders may request a debriefing on the results of the bid solicitation process. Bidders should make the request to the Contracting Authority within 15 working days from receipt of the results of the bid solicitation process. The debriefing may be in writing, by telephone or in person. 9. Official Languages Environment and Climate Change Canada provides procurement services in both official languages. Bidders may submit a bid in the official language of their choice. 10. Additional Information For additional information, interested suppliers must contact the Contracting Officer named in this Notice.
